LoloBuy shopping agent order status: what happens before warehouse entry

A pre-warehouse order status tells you who currently has the next task: you, the purchasing agent, the seller or the warehouse. Reading that handoff correctly prevents unnecessary enquiries and helps you respond when the order really needs a decision.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s current public purchase, shopping-agent status, confirmation, payment-difference and warehouse-entry materials, checked on 16 October 2026. Interface wording can change, and the live order page remains the controlling record.

First identify the right timeline

LoloBuy uses separate records for the seller purchase, the warehouse inventory and the international parcel. This article covers the first timeline only: the shopping-agent order from submission until the item becomes available in My Warehouse. It does not interpret airline, customs or last-mile scans; those belong to the international tracking status guide.

This distinction matters because the same everyday word can describe different work. “Shipped by Seller” means the seller sent the item within China toward LoloBuy’s warehouse. It does not mean the item has left China. “Received” means the warehouse accepted the domestic package, not that the buyer overseas received anything. “In Stock” or “Stored in warehouse” means the item completed the relevant entry process and can be managed from the warehouse inventory.

Before reacting to a status, save the LoloBuy order number, seller link, selected option and date of the latest change. Then check whether the order page contains a payment request, confirmation question or agent message. The label gives context; the action shown on the individual order tells you what to do.

Awaiting Payment: submitted but not funded

The official status page defines Awaiting Payment as an order that has been submitted but not paid. At this point LoloBuy has not confirmed the purchase from the seller. A product sitting at this stage should not be treated as reserved, ordered or protected from a seller price change.

Review the exact option, quantity, product price, Chinese domestic delivery amount, destination country and remarks before paying. If the product link had to be entered manually, compare the submitted record with your saved listing evidence. The manual order guide explains how to preserve the seller’s original option wording and set a clear “do not substitute” condition.

If you no longer want the order, use the current cancellation controls instead of assuming an unpaid entry can be ignored forever. LoloBuy publishes an automatic cancellation rule for unpaid orders, but platform time limits can change. Follow the live countdown or instructions shown in your account.

Processing: payment confirmed and purchasing underway

Processing means LoloBuy has confirmed payment and the purchasing team is working on the seller order. It is not yet proof that the seller accepted the transaction or that the selected item is in stock. The agent may still need to verify an option, a domestic shipping fee, a price change or a seller condition.

Watch for messages rather than submitting duplicate orders. LoloBuy’s purchase guide says buyers can use Order Enquiry during purchasing and that agents may contact them by message or email when more information is required. A concise enquiry should identify the order, state the exact unresolved point and explain the decision you want the agent to follow.

For example: “If the navy XL option is unavailable, please cancel; do not replace it with black.” That is actionable. “Please buy soon” does not resolve stock, price or option ambiguity.

Pending for Confirmation: the order needs your answer

LoloBuy defines Pending for Confirmation as a state in which some item information must be verified again. The official instruction is to read the request on the order page and reply there. This is an action status, not a normal waiting stage.

The question may concern a different price, missing option, seller response, domestic delivery cost or other order detail. Do not approve a vague change simply to move the order forward. Compare the request with the source listing you saved and reply with one clear outcome: accept, reject, cancel, or ask a specific follow-up question.

If the page requests an outstanding balance, verify what changed before paying. LoloBuy’s separate FAQ says an additional amount can result from a seller price change or Chinese domestic delivery fee. That explanation does not prove that every payment request is correct; it tells you which order-level evidence to compare. Check the selected option, seller price and stated domestic delivery amount, then follow the current payment instructions if you accept the difference.

Ordered: the seller is preparing the item

The published LoloBuy shopping agent order status page describes Ordered as the stage after the seller receives the purchase order and prepares to ship. The item has not yet reached LoloBuy. A seller-side delay, pre-order term, customization process or stock problem can still intervene.

Do not interpret Ordered as a warehouse QC result. There are no warehouse photos yet because the warehouse does not have the item. If the listing was a pre-order or customized product, keep the seller’s stated conditions with your records. If the waiting period becomes inconsistent with the current order guidance, use Order Enquiry and ask whether the seller has confirmed stock and dispatch—not whether international tracking is available.

This is also the stage where a requested change becomes harder as work progresses. LoloBuy’s modification FAQ says the platform can try to negotiate a change before seller dispatch, but it does not promise the seller will agree. Once the seller has dispatched, the published route may require waiting for warehouse arrival, arranging a return and placing a new order, with possible domestic return costs.

Shipped by Seller: domestic movement, not international shipping

Shipped by Seller means the seller dispatched the order to LoloBuy’s warehouse. Treat the associated number as Chinese domestic tracking. It can show collection, transit and warehouse delivery, but it is not the future international parcel number.

A single seller order may also arrive in more than one domestic package, or several separately purchased items may reach the warehouse on different days. Do not assume every product in your account will become available together. Match each domestic tracking record to the order and quantity it represents.

LoloBuy publishes domestic-delivery estimates and warehouse-location information, but those details are operational and can age quickly. This guide does not turn them into a deadline. Use the live seller dispatch record, the actual domestic carrier events and the current support guidance. Escalate a clear exception—such as a returned package or an unexplained delivery mismatch—with the tracking number and event text.

Received: signed for, then inspected and entered

The official FAQ explains that Received means the item arrived at the LoloBuy warehouse. The next steps include weighing, inspection and warehouse confirmation. That is why an item can show Received without yet appearing in My Warehouse.

This short gap has a practical purpose. Staff must associate the domestic parcel with the correct order, check the item under the applicable service scope and create the warehouse record. A carrier’s delivered scan alone does not prove that all expected units were identified, inspected and stocked.

Check the order record for an exception or question before contacting support. If the item remains unavailable beyond the current warehouse guidance, send the LoloBuy order number, domestic tracking number, carrier delivery event, item quantity and seller package details. Ask whether the parcel is awaiting identification, inspection or another action. Avoid opening several enquiries for the same delivery, which can fragment the evidence.

In Stock or Stored in warehouse: ready for a warehouse decision

LoloBuy’s public pages use both In Stock and Stored in warehouse for the completed warehouse-entry stage. The wording may differ across help pages or account views, so focus on the practical test: the item appears in My Warehouse and can be selected for later parcel submission.

Stock-in is not a guarantee that the seller sent the correct product or that every hidden characteristic works. Review the warehouse photos and inspection result against the saved order. Standard inspection focuses on visible matters such as style, quantity, colour, size and model, while sealed goods and professional judgments about authenticity, electronics, function or quality have limits.

If the visible evidence matches, you can keep consolidating or plan a parcel. If it shows the wrong option, missing unit or obvious problem, use the current warehouse enquiry or return route before international dispatch. The QC photo checklist provides an approve, question or hold method for that decision.

A status-to-action checklist

  • Awaiting Payment: verify the complete order before funding it.
  • Processing: monitor for an agent question; do not assume seller acceptance.
  • Pending for Confirmation: read the order-level request and answer precisely.
  • Ordered: the seller is preparing the item; warehouse evidence does not exist yet.
  • Shipped by Seller: follow Chinese domestic tracking, not international tracking.
  • Received: the warehouse signed for the package and is completing entry work.
  • In Stock / Stored in warehouse: review photos and inspection, then decide whether to consolidate, return or submit a parcel.

At every stage, record the last status change and any accompanying message. Ask for help when the order shows a clear exception, requests information or no longer matches the current guidance. Lead with evidence and one answerable question rather than a general demand for speed.

Conclusion: follow the handoff, not just the label

A LoloBuy shopping agent order status is most useful when you connect it to the responsible party. Awaiting Payment belongs to the buyer; Processing to the purchasing team; Ordered and Shipped by Seller to the seller-side handoff; Received to warehouse intake; and In Stock to your next warehouse decision. Pending for Confirmation interrupts that sequence because your reply is required.

Keep the product record, order number and domestic tracking evidence together, and never confuse seller dispatch with international shipment. Once the item is stocked, review the QC evidence before creating a parcel. For product research before ordering, open FindSpreadsheet →
